story.head: The Lightning are going to let it fly
paras: The Lightning (8-3-1) beat Winnipeg 6-4 on Thursday, while the Predators (4-4-5) lost 4-3 to Washington the same night. Going in, the Lightning are fourth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Predators sixth in the Central (tied for 22nd).

The Lightning get into more chippy games than anyone (1st), rarely ice the puck (2nd) and keep shots away from their net (3rd). The Predators, by contrast, keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). They also get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (30th). The Bolts are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators.

Brandon Hagel (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 12 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with four goals in six games against Nashville since 2023-24. Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 12 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. Steven Stamkos (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 13 GP) is tied for the Predators’ scoring lead. Filip Forsberg (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 13 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games.
Andrei Vasilevskiy (6-3-0 / .876 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Tampa Bay, and Juuse Saros (3-3-4 / .902 SV% in 10 GS) for Nashville.
The Lightning usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.
